# QYL0304: EventSource instrumentation is trimmed under Native AOT without EventSourceSupport

<!-- <auto-generated /> This file is generated by tools/Qyl.Telemetry.SemanticConventions.Analyzers.DocsGenerator. -->

| Property | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Severity | Warning |
| Category | `Configuration` |
| Code fix | No |
| Analyzer | `Qyl0304EnableEventSourceSupportAnalyzer` |
| Enabled by default | Yes |

## Description

Under Native AOT with EventSourceSupport unset, the runtime trims EventSource/EventPipe to a no-op: any in-process EventSource, EventListener, or EventCounter — including OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EventCounters — silently stops emitting at runtime, with no build error. This rule fires only when such instrumentation is present in the compilation together with PublishAot=true and EventSourceSupport unset, so it does not flag the common OTLP-push app. OpenTelemetry's OTLP export (ActivitySource plus Meter/MeterListener) does not use EventSource and is unaffected; enabling EventSourceSupport increases Native AOT output size, so enable it only when you rely on EventPipe-based instrumentation. The out-of-process case (dotnet-trace/dotnet-counters) is not detectable at compile time and is out of scope.
